items.abstract: <jats:p>Contemporary agentic AI systems face critical challenges in tool orchestration, dynamic coordination, and framework interoperability. I present FATA (Framework Agnostic and Task Agnostic Agentic AI), a novel control plane design pattern that enables scalable, distributed multi-agent orchestration through serverless architecture. FATA introduces a unified tool management layer that dynamically routes, validates, and governs tool interactions while maintaining framework independence. My approach distinguishes between specialized AI agents for targeted automation and collaborative agentic ecosystems with emergent collective intelligence. Through systematic evaluation across cybersecurity, compliance, and document processing domains, FATA demonstrates the capability to reduce developer complexity, enable runtime adaptability, and provide robust governance mechanisms for enterprise-scale agentic deployments.</jats:p>
title: FATA: A Framework-Agnostic, Task-Agnostic Agentic AI Platform for Serverless Multi-Agent Orchestration

items.abstract: <jats:p>The Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) sector has been undergoing rapid digital transformation. While extended reality (XR) technologies have demonstrated potential to enhance AEC education, the growing volume of XR-related research has made synthesis increasingly challenging. Traditional review methodologies remain largely static. Recent advances in agentic large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to address this limitation by enabling dialogue-driven reasoning over structured data. The aim of this study is to develop and evaluate an integrated human-in-the-loop agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework that transforms contextualized structured review data into an interactive, query-driven knowledge system. To validate the framework, a systematic review of XR applications in AEC education was conducted, resulting in a dataset of 59 peer-reviewed studies published between 2014 and 2023. The studies were organized using a schema-first data organization strategy. An agentic AI application was then implemented using a Streamlit-based interface integrated with LLMs, enabling controlled natural-language querying and visual analytics without model training or fine-tuning. Application performance was evaluated across quantitative and qualitative questions. Progressive grounding and model refinement reduced quantitative error rates from over 50% to 0.00% for single- and two-aspect questions and to 3.23% for three-aspect questions, while qualitative error rates were reduced to 0.00%. The application reproduced all manually identified bibliometric patterns and uniquely enabled scenario-based, multi-attribute reasoning. Future work will generalize the framework into a deployable tool for arbitrary structured datasets beyond XR, supporting multi-value reasoning and broader adoption of agentic LLM-based knowledge systems.</jats:p>
title: An Integrated Human-in-the-loop Agentic Artificial Intelligence Framework for Analyzing Contextualized Structured Data

items.abstract: <jats:p>Advances in LLMs are driving structural changes across the software development landscape, particularly in software product development processes. These transformations extend beyond programming and increasingly influence established UI design workflows. Conventional UI design relies on iterative cycles of prototyping and user testing. However, such processes are often time- and resource-intensive, creating tension with real-world environments that demand rapid iteration. Although prior research has explored AI-assisted approaches to support UI design, most studies focus on isolated functionalities or depend on code-based inputs that are rarely available in practical design settings. To address these limitations, this study proposes Vibe Design, an LLM-based agentic framework that enables iterative interface prototyping and usability test simulation without relying on code-based data. The framework integrates LLM-assisted prototyping and usability test simulation grounded in the Persona-Scenario-Goal methodology. An empirical study was conducted using three types of user data, namely demographic profiles, persona descriptions, and interview transcripts, to evaluate simulation performance. Results indicate that the interview-based agent achieved the highest performance, reproducing 76% of the usability themes identified in human usability testing. By integrating the Persona-Scenario-Goal methodology and Human-in-the-Loop mechanisms, this study demonstrates both the practical applicability and methodological implications for LLM-based UI design agents. While the findings highlight the potential of AI-driven user simulation to reduce repetitive validation costs, they also indicate that higher-order judgment and creative reframing remain the domain of human designers. These results underscore the need for complementary human-AI collaboration in the reconfiguration of contemporary design processes.</jats:p>
title: Vibe Design: Human-in-the-loop Agentic Framework for UI Design with Large Language Models
